title: Idiomatic C# after five years (style that scales)
hook: Idiomatic C# is not clever code — it is code other .NET engineers read without friction: async all the way for I/O, sealed by default, composition over inheritance, pattern matching over nested ifs, and names that match the Base Class Library (BCL).

blocks.text: After five years you default to: IAsyncEnumerable for streaming, records for immutable DTOs, early returns, guard clauses, Dependency Injection constructor injection, and ConfigureAwait(false) in libraries. You avoid Hungarian notation, underscore prefixes on locals, and Java-style getters in favor of properties. You use var when the type is obvious from the right-hand side.

entries.plainDefinition: Core .NET APIs shipped with the runtime (System.*).
entries.example: List<T>, Task, Span<T> — naming follows BCL patterns.

entries.plainDefinition: Early validation that returns or throws before main logic.
Prevents further inheritance — default for classes not designed as base classes.

blocks.text: Code review at senior level is about readability and failure modes, not syntax trivia. Idiomatic services use async Redis, return Result types instead of exceptions for expected failures (module 09), and keep controllers thin. Matching Microsoft naming guidelines makes onboarding faster — critical for teams shipping microservices.

blocks.title: Read like the BCL
blocks.body: Before inventing a pattern, check how System.Text.Json or ASP.NET Core does it — that is the style bar.

snippet.label: Guard clauses and early return
snippet.explanation: Validate first, happy path reads top-to-bottom without deep nesting.

snippet.label: Pattern over nested if
snippet.explanation: Switch expression exhaustiveness is clearer than if-else chains for typed errors.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Java-style GetUser/setUser instead of User property. public fields on DTOs. God classes with 2000 lines. Blocking async (.Result) in ASP.NET handlers.

interviewTakeaways: Idiomatic = async I/O, sealed classes, records, patterns, guard clauses.
Match BCL naming and composition patterns.
Readability and failure modes beat clever one-liners.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Early return, readonly data, async handlers — same readability goals as idiomatic C# services.
